newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New York Times business - Oct 4.

text.p: The New York Times reported the following business stories on Friday:
* Dickson Concepts (International) Ltd has made an initial offer to buy Barney's Inc for between $300 million and $400 million.
* Ford Motor Co said sales of its cars and light trucks rose 7.3 percent in September, compared to a 5.9 percent increase for U.S. auto makers overall.
* Italy's Olivetti SpA said it planned to sell its personal computer division as part of a sale of assets designed to raise between $655 million and $785 million.

* New York City asked Time Warner Inc if it could carry News Corp Ltd's 24-hour Fox news channel on a public access cable station that the city controls. Time Warner, whose franchise as the city's cable television provider expires in 1998, refused.
* Negotiations between General Motors Corp and the Canadian Automobile Workers union showed little progress as thousands of assembly workers went on strike.
* Eastman Kodak Co is in negotiations with Wang Laboratories to buy Wang's document imaging software business.
* Kohlberg Kravis Roberts & Co has agreed to buy KinderCare Learning Centers Inc for about $467 million, or $20.25 a share.

* Authentic Fitness Corp is abandoning the ski wear business, closing its outlet stores and restating its third and fourth quarter results to include additional reserves to cover potential losses on inventory and accounts receivable.
* The U.S. government presented a pension fund rescue plan to protect employers, taxpayers and union retirees in the men's suit industry.
* U.S. treasury securities prices were generally lower Thursday as the market awaited Friday's monthly employment figures. It ignored a report of a larger than projected drop in factory orders.
